docs.title: Anatomy of a component
docs.text:
<AskOne id="choose-approach" question="How should I build this feature?" subagent="Use the smallest change.">
- Smallest change (Recommended): touch as little as possible
- Refactor first: clean the area up
</AskOne>
Part What it does id Becomes the anchor in the contents list, so a model can jump straight here question Props become variables inside the component, and can use values from Jinja2, which runs first subagent Says what a subagent should do instead, since it cannot reach the user The tag's content Becomes children. Put your recommendation first Why two passes, Jinja2 and then components?

Jinja2 runs first, so <Backoff retries="{{ retries }}" /> receives a real number. Components then expand, innermost first, so a <Tab> is ready by the time <AskTabs> uses it. The contents list comes last, because only then are the line numbers known.

What happens to tags in code examples?

They are left alone. The <Flow> in a code fence or in inline code stays exactly as written, so a skill can show examples of them.

Do these force a model to behave?

No. They are instructions, and a model can still ignore text. On a real model the question types, task lists, plans, formatting rules, the subagent flow and live sections all worked as intended, which you can check with scripts/gate_ui_templates.sh. Anything that must hold needs a real check, such as a task's --check command.

docs.title: Make your own
docs.text:
• Copy .agent/template/demo.mdx to a new name, and change name: to match
  • Keep the components you need, and delete the rest
  • Preview with aiculator template --render NAME
  • Install with aiculator template --install NAME
  • Add aiculator template --check to CI, so that a changed template cannot go stale unnoticed

Or start smaller with aiculator template --new my-rules. See Templates for the full reference.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Templates let you write instructions once and reuse them. Use them for the rules you keep repeating: when to use subagents, how to retry, what format to reply in, and which steps to follow.

Instructions, not enforcement

A template produces text for a model, and a model can still ignore text. Clear, specific rules are followed far more often, but anything that must hold needs a real check, such as a task's --check command.

See every feature working together

The template demo walks through one template that uses all of this.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
aiculator template --list
aiculator template --render agent-discipline --set retries=5   # Preview; writes nothing
aiculator template --install agent-discipline                  # Render and install

--install takes the same options as skill --install: patterns, --harness, --global, --path and --copy.

docs.title: Where templates live
docs.text:
Templates go in .agents/templates/. .agent/templates/ and .agent/template/ also work.

.agents/templates/
├── my-rules.md.j2            # A single-file template
├── release-flow/             # A template with extra files
│   ├── SKILL.md.j2
│   └── references/guide.md   # Copied into the skill
├── partials/                 # For {% include %}
└── components/               # Your own <Components>

Single files can end in .md.j2, .j2, .jinja or .mdx.

docs.title: Anatomy of a template
docs.text:
---
template:                 # Removed from the output
  vars:
    retries: 3
name: my-rules
description: Working rules for this project. Use when the user asks to apply them.
metadata:
  version: "1.0.0"
---

# My rules

<Toc />

<Directive id="main-rule">Never push to main.</Directive>

{% if harness.id == "claude" %}
This line appears only in the Claude Code copy.
{% endif %}

{% include "partials/house-style.md" %}

<Backoff timeout="120s" retries="{{ retries }}" />

Rendering runs in two passes: Jinja2 first, then components. So {{ retries }} can feed a component's props.

docs.title: Subagents
docs.text:
Says when to use subagents.

<Subagents use="when" max="4"
  when="the work splits into independent parts"
  not_when="the steps depend on each other" />

use is always, when or never.

docs.title: Backoff
docs.text:
Sets a command timeout and a retry policy. The swarm computes the table of waits, because a model told to "double it each time" tends to get the numbers wrong.

<Backoff timeout="120s" retries="3" base="2s" factor="2" limit="60s" />

Add on="..." to say which failures to retry.

docs.title: OutputFormat
docs.text:
Makes the model repeat a format in every reply.

<OutputFormat>
Done: what changed
Checked: what you ran and the result
</OutputFormat>

Use repeat="Final answers" to apply it to only some replies.

docs.title: Flow and Step
docs.text:
Forces an order of steps, with interactive questions and exceptions for subagents, which cannot reach the user.

<Flow name="confirm before acting" id="confirm-flow">
<Step n="1" title="Plan" id="plan"
  ask="Does this plan look right?"
  subagent="Do not ask. Continue, and report your plan with the result.">
List the changes you intend to make.
</Step>
</Flow>

docs.title: Directive
docs.text:
Marks a rule the model can cite by name. level is any word, and defaults to must.

<Directive level="must not" id="no-false-claims">Say something works unless you ran it.</Directive>

docs.title: Toc and Anchor
docs.text:
<Toc /> writes a table of contents with exact line numbers and anchors, so a model can jump to a section without reading the whole file:

## Contents

- Subagents: line 28, anchor `subagents`
- Commands: timeouts and retries: line 39, anchor `backoff`

<Anchor id="name" /> adds a searchable marker anywhere. Most components add their own.

docs.title: Note
docs.text: <Note>Something worth pointing out.</Note>

docs.title: Forcing a kind of question
docs.text:
Bundled templates tell a model which interface to use, so you get a list to select from, and not a paragraph to answer.

Template Component What the user sees ui-select <AskOne> One choice from a list ui-checkbox <AskMany> Any number of choices, as checkboxes ui-tabs <AskTabs> and <Tab> Several questions in one form, with tabs ui-confirm <AskConfirm> A yes or no choice before a risky action ui-text <AskText> A place to type, when options cannot cover the answer ui-preview <AskPreview> Choices with a visible example of each ui-todos <TodoList> A live task list ui-plan <PlanMode> A plan to approve before anything changes 
aiculator template --install 'ui-*'
aiculator template --install 'ui-*' --per-harness --harness claude,opencode   # Names the exact tool

They name the harness's real tool and settings when it has one, and that comes from each harness's docs:

Harness Questions Task list Plan mode Claude Code AskUserQuestion, with multiSelect TaskCreate, TaskUpdate EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode Gemini CLI ask_user, with type choice, text or yesno write_todos enter_plan_mode, exit_plan_mode OpenCode question; its docs do not state multi-select todowrite None in its tool docs Others None named: a numbered list, then stop and wait A Markdown checklist A numbered plan, then stop and wait

On some Claude Code models the task tools must be switched on, so ui-todos also tells the model what to do without them. Whether AskUserQuestion offers preview depends on the session, so <AskPreview> falls back to labeled code blocks.

ui-plan deliberately has no allowed-tools. In Claude Code that field skips the permission prompt, and the prompt on ExitPlanMode is your approval of the plan.

Without --per-harness, one shared skill names all three tools, because it cannot know which harness reads it.

To ask a specific question, use the components in your own template:

<AskOne question="Which database?" subagent="Use SQLite, and say so in your report.">
- PostgreSQL (Recommended): best for most apps
- SQLite: no server to run
</AskOne>

<AskMany question="Which checks should I run?" min="1">
- Unit tests
- Security scan
</AskMany>

<AskTabs>
<Tab header="Language" question="Which language?">Go, or Python</Tab>
<Tab header="Extras" question="Which extras?" multi="true">Docker, or CI</Tab>
</AskTabs>

<AskConfirm question="Delete 3 merged branches?" />

<AskText question="What should the service be called?" placeholder="my-service" />

<AskPreview question="Which layout?">
- Compact: `a | b`
- Spacious: `a  |  b`
</AskPreview>

<TodoList>
- Write the tests
- Make them pass
</TodoList>

<PlanMode>
- Which files change
- How you will verify it
</PlanMode>

Every question also covers two cases: a harness with no question tool, and a subagent that cannot reach the user.

docs.title: Forcing rich Markdown
docs.text:
rich-markdown sets how a model formats its replies, using the right form for each thing. <RichMarkdown> includes every rule below, and <Render> adds a single one.

aiculator template --install rich-markdown                    # For a terminal
aiculator template --install rich-markdown --set surface=rich # Where full Markdown renders

<RichMarkdown only="code,diff,table,fileref" surface="terminal" />

<Render kind="callout">Use this for production warnings only.</Render>
kind What the model is told With surface="terminal" (the default) With surface="rich" code Fenced block with a language Same Same inline code, bold and italics, for the right things Same Same shell A sh block to paste, with output apart Same Same diff A diff block Same Same table Comparisons, with short cells Same Same list Numbered when order matters Same Same checklist - [ ] and - [x] Same Same headings ## and ### for longer answers Same Same callout A quote with a bold label Same Also GitHub's > [!WARNING] quote Exact errors, logs and documents Same Same fileref path/to/file.go:42 Same Same tree A directory layout in a text block Same Same link Descriptive text, and only URLs it has seen Same Same diagram Flows and relationships ASCII in a text block A mermaid block image Pictures A path and a description ![alt](path) details Long optional material Left out, or at the end <details> math Formulas Plain text or code $...$ and $$...$$ footnote Asides and sources Short sentences and links [^1] rule Separate parts of a reply Same Same

An unknown kind fails the render, so a typo cannot silently drop a rule.

What this controls, and what it does not

These rules decide what the model writes. How it then looks depends on your harness and where it runs, which most harnesses do not document. Terminal rules are the cautious default for that reason, so check a sample in your own harness before you set surface=rich.

A long skill can keep its contents list short with <Toc depth="2" />, which lists only the ## sections.

docs.title: Subagent flows
docs.text:
subagent-flow makes a model act as an orchestrator: it runs stages in order, delegates each one, and checks each result before moving on.

<SubagentFlow name="research, build, review">
<Stage n="1" title="Research" parallel="3"
  output="Short findings with file paths" done="you could explain the change">
Split the unknowns into separate questions.
</Stage>

<Stage n="2" title="Review" agent="a fresh subagent that did not write the code"
  done="each problem is fixed or explained">
Ask it to look for bugs.
</Stage>
</SubagentFlow>

docs.title: Sections a model keeps current
docs.text:
<DynamicSection> marks text the model must keep true as it works. living-section is a ready-made one, for a progress file.

<DynamicSection id="status" title="Status" file="PROGRESS.md"
  update="after every commit"
  keep="what is done, what is blocked, and the next step" />

With file, the section lives in that project file, which is usually what you want. Without it, the section lives in the skill itself, between markers:

<DynamicSection id="decisions" title="Decisions so far">Nothing yet.</DynamicSection>

Re-rendering keeps what a model wrote there, and --check does not count it as drift. A model's edit can shift the line numbers in a contents list until the next render, though the anchors stay right.

docs.title: How well this works
docs.text:
These are instructions, so a model can still ignore them. scripts/gate_ui_templates.sh tests them on a real Claude Code session, using Haiku, the cheapest model:

Probe Result on the real model ui-select One call with multiSelect: false, recommendation first ui-checkbox One call with multiSelect: true ui-tabs One call holding 3 questions No question tool Looks for the tool, then writes the numbered list As a subagent Does not ask, and reports its choice living-section Writes PROGRESS.md with the markers subagent-flow Three subagents, including a separate reviewer, and the bug fixed ui-confirm One choice, Delete build directory or Keep it, before acting ui-text Asks in its reply, and creates nothing ui-preview Every option carries a preview ui-todos TaskCreate per step, and TaskUpdate as each one starts and ends ui-plan Presents a numbered plan, and changes no file rich-markdown A diff block, a sh block, a table and calc.go:3 in one reply

Print mode has nobody to answer, so Claude Code does not offer AskUserQuestion there. For the mode probes, a small server offers a tool with the same name and schema, and records the arguments. So this proves what the model asks for, but not how the real interactive UI looks. Other harnesses have not been tested this way.

Two more limits follow from this. The ui-plan probe proves the plan comes first and nothing changes, but not the real EnterPlanMode tool, which the model did not call in print mode. The rich-markdown probe checks the text the model wrote, not how a terminal displays it.

docs.title: Your own components
docs.text:
Create components/Name.md in a template directory, using Jinja2. Props become variables, and the tag's content becomes children. A project component with a bundled name replaces the bundled one.

.agents/templates/components/Warn.md
> **Warning{% if topic is defined %} about {{ topic }}{% endif %}:** {{ children | trim }}

<Warn topic="deploys">Check the staging logs first.</Warn>

Tags inside code fences and inline code are left alone, so you can show examples.

docs.title: Per-harness copies
docs.text:
A skill installed the normal way is one file shared through links, so harness.id is generic in it. To vary by harness, render a separate copy into each harness's own directory:

aiculator template --install my-rules --per-harness --harness claude,opencode
aiculator template --render my-rules --for claude     # Preview one
Variable Value harness.id, harness.name Which harness, or generic harness.has_mcp, harness.has_acp What it supports harness.reads_agents Whether it reads .agents/skills harness.question_tool Its question tool, if confirmed; empty otherwise skill.name The template's name aiculator.version The running version

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• Rendering cannot run code or read outside the template directories, so rendering a template from an untrusted repository does not endanger your machine. What the skill then tells a model to do still deserves review.
  • A typo in a variable name is an error, and it does not silently render as nothing.
  • A render is linted first. A template with a mistake cannot damage an installed skill.
  • Hand-written skills are never overwritten. Only directories a template generated are replaced.

docs.title: Keep skills current
docs.text:
Rendered skills are ordinary files, so a changed template leaves them stale. This fails if any have drifted, which suits CI:

aiculator template --check

docs.title: Run sandboxed workers
docs.text:
aiculator drive launches a harness for you over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), one session per task, inside the sandbox.

SWARM_TOKEN=$(aiculator token --agent worker1 --tier 1) \
  aiculator drive --harness claude --agent worker1

docs.title: Why use it
docs.text:
• Idle time costs nothing. No harness runs until there is a task, so waiting uses no model turns.
  • It is sandboxed. The harness can write only to its worktree, a private temp directory and its own state directories. It cannot read the swarm's secrets or credential stores such as ~/.ssh.
  • Permissions follow a policy. Reads, searches and commands are allowed because the sandbox contains them. Edits must stay inside the worktree. Unknown tool kinds are refused.

docs.title: Useful flags
docs.text: Flag Purpose --max-tasks N Stop after N tasks. --manifest file.yaml Use a harness that is not in the registry. --sandbox docker Choose the sandbox. none turns it off, and must be asked for by name. --heartbeat 15s How often to save work and renew the lease.

docs.title: A custom harness
docs.text:
my-harness.yaml
name: my-harness
command: [my-harness, --acp]
pass_env: [MY_API_KEY]
real_home: true
write_paths: ["~/.my-harness"]
denied_tools: [fetch]

docs.title: When a harness cannot work
docs.text: A missing login or a failed launch hands the task back with no penalty and stops that driver. It does not use up the task's attempts or move it to a pricier tier.

docs.title: Which harnesses have been run
docs.text:
Claude Code and OpenCode have run this way for real. The others are configured from their documentation or the ACP registry and are untested. To test one:

./scripts/gate3_real.sh gemini 3

docs.title: Package managers
docs.text:
Each release runs .github/workflows/packages.yml. Every channel installs the real package first, then publishes it if the release is not a prerelease and the channel's secrets are set. A channel with no secrets is skipped with a notice, and one channel failing does not stop the others.

Nothing is published yet

These channels need the one-time setup below. Until a channel has published, the install commands for it will not work.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Channel How it publishes Secrets Needs first Homebrew Commits to your tap PACKAGING_TOKEN Repository homebrew-aiculator Scoop Commits to your bucket PACKAGING_TOKEN Repository scoop-aiculator apt, dnf, apk Signed repositories on GitHub Pages PACKAGING_TOKEN, PACKAGE_GPG_KEY, APK_SIGNING_KEY Repository aiculator-packages, with Pages on Chocolatey choco push CHOCOLATEY_API_KEY A community.chocolatey.org account WinGet Pull request to microsoft/winget-pkgs WINGET_TOKEN Nothing Arch User Repository Pushes aiculator-bin AUR_SSH_KEY An aur.archlinux.org account with this public key

apt, dnf and apk have no central registry that accepts a project directly, so these repositories are hosted by the project. Getting into Debian, Fedora or Alpine themselves means going through each distribution's own review.

Two channels have human review. Chocolatey moderates package versions before listing them, and each WinGet version is a pull request that is reviewed before it merges. Both can take days, while the other channels are live after the workflow finishes.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
gh repo create Grano22/homebrew-aiculator --public --add-readme
gh repo create Grano22/scoop-aiculator --public --add-readme
gh repo create Grano22/aiculator-packages --public --add-readme
gh api -X POST repos/Grano22/aiculator-packages/pages \
  -f build_type=legacy -f 'source[branch]=main' -f 'source[path]=/'

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text:
• PACKAGING_TOKEN: a fine-grained token, limited to the three repositories above, with Contents: read and write.
  • WINGET_TOKEN: a classic token, because it must fork and open a pull request on a repository you do not own. See wingetcreate's token guide for its scope.
  • CHOCOLATEY_API_KEY: from your account page on community.chocolatey.org.

docs.title: Signing keys
docs.text:
Generate these on a trusted machine. They have no passphrase, because CI has to use them unattended, so the repository secret is what protects them.

export GNUPGHOME=$(mktemp -d)
gpg --batch --passphrase '' --quick-generate-key "Aiculator packages" ed25519 sign 5y
gpg --batch --armor --export-secret-keys | gh secret set PACKAGE_GPG_KEY -R Grano22/aiculator
openssl genrsa 4096 | gh secret set APK_SIGNING_KEY -R Grano22/aiculator
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N '' -C aiculator-aur -f aur_ed25519
gh secret set AUR_SSH_KEY -R Grano22/aiculator < aur_ed25519

Add aur_ed25519.pub to your AUR account, then delete both files and $GNUPGHOME.

Keep a safe copy of the GPG and apk keys if you want the option to restore them. Replacing either key later means every user has to trust the new one.

docs.title: Try it without publishing
docs.text:
gh workflow run packages.yml -R Grano22/aiculator -f dry_run=true            # The latest release
gh workflow run packages.yml -R Grano22/aiculator -f tag=v0.4.0 -f dry_run=false   # Retry a release for real

A dry run installs from every channel using throwaway signing keys. Pull requests that change the packaging run one automatically. Publishing again is safe, since each channel notices a version it already has.

macOS and LinuxWindowsDebian and UbuntuFedora and RHELAlpineArch

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Windows on Arm: Chocolatey installs the x64 build. Scoop and WinGet have native arm64 builds.
  • Old versions: the apt, dnf and apk repositories keep the newest 5 versions, and keep no git history, so that they stay within GitHub Pages' size limits.
  • macOS signing: the binaries are not notarized by Apple.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: Releases are driven by semantic version tags. scripts/release.sh creates the tag, and pushing it does the rest.

docs.title: Make a release
docs.text:
1. Keep CHANGELOG.md current as you work, under ## [Unreleased].

  2. Preview:

    scripts/release.sh --bump minor --dry-run

  3. Create and publish:

    scripts/release.sh --bump minor --push
Flag Meaning --bump major\|minor\|patch The next version, from the latest stable tag --version X.Y.Z An exact version --pre rc.1 A prerelease, such as v1.2.0-rc.1 --push Push the commit and tag, which publishes --dry-run Show what would happen, and change nothing --allow-branch Release from a branch other than master --skip-tests Skip the local tests; CI still runs them

Without --push, nothing leaves your machine, and the script prints how to undo it.

The script refuses a version that is not semantic or already exists, an empty [Unreleased] section, and uncommitted changes.

docs.title: What a tag does
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    T[Push tag v1.2.3] --> V[Verify tag, notes and tests]
    V --> B[Build 8 platforms]
    B --> P[Publish release]
    T --> D[Publish docs 1.2 and latest]
  • Binaries: Linux, macOS, Windows and FreeBSD, each on amd64 and arm64.
  • Each archive includes the third-party license notices, which the dependency licenses require.
  • Also published: SHA256SUMS, build provenance attestations, and notes taken from that version's changelog section.
  • Prereleases are marked as such on GitHub, and do not change the latest docs.

Check an archive's provenance with:

gh attestation verify aiculator_v1.2.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz --repo OWNER/REPO

docs.title: Size budget
docs.text:
scripts/build_release.sh fails if a binary or an archive goes over budget, so neither CI nor a release can ship past it.

Package Budget Current Binary 30 MiB 24.6 to 27.7 MiB Archive 11 MiB 9.0 to 10.5 MiB

The template engine accounts for about 5.4 MiB of the binary, because real Jinja2 brings text-handling and JSON libraries with it. To raise a limit, change it in the script on purpose and say why in the commit.

docs.text:

docs.title: Set up a new repository
docs.text:
These are one-time steps on GitHub:

  1. Pages: in Settings, set the source to the gh-pages branch. It appears after the first docs run.
  2. Actions: in Settings, allow workflows to read and write, so that releases and docs can publish.
  3. Snyk: add a SNYK_TOKEN repository secret. Until then, that scan is skipped.
  4. CodeQL: code scanning results need a public repository or GitHub Advanced Security. The same goes for attestations on a private repository.
  5. Branch protection: require the CI checks on master.

Dependabot starts on its own from .github/dependabot.yml.

  aiculator template --install x --per-harness       a separate copy per harness

  aiculator template --check                         fail if a rendered skill is stale

      --list              list templates
      --new string        create a starter template

docs.title: aiculator top
docs.text:
Live terminal dashboard: flow, throughput, latency, jitter, probes, liveness and usage

A live view of the swarm. Keys: 1-5 or tab switch views, arrows or j and k scroll, p pauses, q quits.

Without a terminal, such as in a pipe, it prints one frame and exits. Rates reset when the server restarts. Task states and usage totals do not.

aiculator top [flags]

Flags

      --color               with --once: keep color even in a pipe
      --interval duration   how often to refresh (default 1s)
      --json                print the raw snapshot as JSON and exit
      --no-color            no color; NO_COLOR also works
      --once                print one frame and exit
      --view string         with --once: overview, tasks, agents, flow or usage (default "overview")
      --width int           with --once: width in columns
